title: Pure dimension of fibres of a flat family with dense pure-dimensional generic fibre
statement: Let $S$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] with generic point $\eta$ [def-sc-generic-point], and let $f:X\to S$ be a flat morphism [def-weil-flat-morphism] locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose that the generic fibre $X_\eta$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is dense in $X$ and that, for an integer $d\geq0$, every irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $X_\eta$ has Krull dimension $d$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Then every nonempty fibre $X_s$ is pure of dimension $d$, meaning that each of its irreducible components has dimension $d$. The same holds for every nonempty geometric fibre $X_s\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, where $s\in S$ and $\Omega$ is any algebraically closed extension of its residue field $\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-residue-field, def-pc-fibre-product]. The empty scheme is allowed as $X$, in which case the conclusions are vacuous.

source.place: Tag 0GSK, remark-flat-equidimensional, second list, with F=O_X; consequence of Tag 0GSJ, lemma-flat-associated-equidimensional. Geometric fibres: literature/stacks-project/morphisms.tex, Tag 02NK, lemma-base-change-relative-dimension-d, with relative dimension defined in Tag 02NJ.

proof.text: Fix $s\in S$ and an irreducible component $C$ of $X_s$. By sobriety choose its generic point $x$, regarded also as a point of $X$ using the fibre homeomorphism. Choose affine neighbourhoods $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $s$ and $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset f^{-1}(V)$ of $x$. The affine flatness criterion makes $A\to R$ flat. Since $S$ is integral, $A$ is a domain and $\eta\in V$ corresponds to $(0)$. If $\mathfrak q$ represents $x$ and $\mathfrak p$ represents $s$, going down applied to $(0)\subseteq\mathfrak p$ and $\mathfrak q$ gives $\mathfrak q_0\subseteq\mathfrak q$ contracting to $(0)$. Thus there is a point $y\in X_\eta$ specializing to $x$ in $X$.

source.place: Tag 00HS (lemma-flat-going-down), applied on affine charts; More on Morphisms Tag 0GSK, second list

proof.text: Choose an irreducible component $B$ of $X_\eta$ containing $y$, using the component-cover theorem, and let $z$ be its generic point by sobriety. In the fibre $z$ specializes to $y$; its continuous inclusion into $X$ shows that $z$ specializes to $x$ in $X$. Put $Z=\overline{\{z\}}$ in $X$ and $Z_s=Z\cap f^{-1}(s)$. This is closed in $X_s$ and contains $x$, hence contains $C=\overline{\{x\}}$ in $X_s$. Any irreducible subset of $Z_s$ properly containing $C$ would also be an irreducible subset of $X_s$ properly containing $C$. Maximality of $C$ therefore makes $C$ an irreducible component of $Z_s$.

source.place: Tag 0GSK (remark-flat-equidimensional), second list: reduction to the closure of a generic-fibre component

proof.text: Apply the fibre-component-closure dimension lemma to the original flat, locally finite type map $f$, to $t=\eta$, to the generic point $z$ of $B$, and to the component $C$ of $Z_s$ found in step 2. It gives $\dim C=\dim B=d$, where the final equality is the hypothesis on the generic fibre. Since $s$ and $C$ were arbitrary, every nonempty ordinary fibre is pure of dimension $d$. This application does not assume that the reduced closure $Z$ is itself flat.

By locally-finite-type base change, $X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is locally of finite type. Apply the pure-open local-dimension lemma to $Y=X_s$, its whole open subset $O=X_s$, and $n=d$. Step 3 supplies every component dimension, so the local topological dimension $\dim_x X_s$ equals $d$ at every $x\in X_s$.

Let $\Omega/\kappa(s)$ be any algebraically closed extension and put $S'=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, mapped to $S$ through $s$. Apply the fibre-dimension-after-base-change theorem to $f$ and this map. Its fibre identification identifies the fibre over the unique point of $S'$ with $G=X_s\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. For every $x'\in G$ with image $x\in X_s$, the theorem gives $\dim_{x'}G=\dim_x X_s=d$ by step 4. Thus the local dimension is constantly $d$ on $G$.

source.place: Tag 02FY (lemma-dimension-fibre-after-base-change), part (1); this is the pointwise input to Tag 02NK

proof.text: The structure morphism $G\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is locally of finite type by base change. A field is Noetherian because its only ideals are $0$ and the unit ideal; hence its spectrum is locally Noetherian by definition. The locally-finite-type over locally-Noetherian theorem therefore makes $G$ locally Noetherian. Apply the constant-local-dimension component theorem with $Y=G$, $O=G$, $n=d$ and step 5: every irreducible component of $G$ has dimension $d$. This proves the geometric-fibre assertion. If $X$ or one of the fibres is empty, it has no irreducible components and the assertions are vacuous.
